chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the husband and wife who both die, so the inheritors of the woman come and claim the dower upon the inheritors of the man. He said: 'And they had both died and the inheritance was distributed?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.'

I said: 'And if the woman was alive, and she came after the death of her husband to claim her dower?' He said: 'There is nothing for her, and she had stayed with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband died.'

I said: 'And if she died while he was alive, so her inheritors came seeking her dower from him?' He said: 'And she had stayed with him until she died not seeking it?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.'
I said: 'And if he divorced her, so she came seeking her dower?' He said: 'And she had stayed not seeking it until he divorced her, there is nothing for her.'

I said: 'So when is the limit of that which, if she were to seek it, it would be for her?' He said: 'If it was gifted to her and she entered his house, then she seeks it after that, so there is nothing for her.'
It is sufficient for her if she makes him swear an oath by Allah that there is no dower for her with him, neither little nor much.

key_terms.تَسْتَحْلِفَ: To make him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: When do the heirs of a wife lose the right to claim her dower after her husband's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'sukut' (silence) as a form of implied acceptance of debt, establishing that a wife's failure to claim her dower (mahr) during the marriage constitutes a waiver of the right to sue for it after his death or divorce. It distinguishes between the full claimable amount and the residual right to exact an oath of non-payment once the marital bond is dissolved, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on preventing perpetual financial liability for the husband. This ruling underscores the Shia view that dower is a right of the wife that can be extinguished by her inaction, contrasting with some Sunni schools that view it as a fixed debt.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahma Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the husband and the wife who both died. So the inheritors of the woman came over claiming the dower upon the inheritors of the man. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They had both died and the inheritances had been distributed?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing for them’.

I said, ‘And if it was such that the woman was alive, so she goes over after the death of her husband to claim her dower?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said : ‘There is nothing for her, and she had stayed with him agreeably until her husband died’.

So I said, ‘Supposing if she had died and he was alive, so her inheritors come over seeking her dower from him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She had stayed with him until he dies and did not seek it?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing for them’.
I said, ‘Supposing he had divorced her, so she came over seeking her dower?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And she had stayed not seeking it until he divorced her, there is nothing for her’.

I said, ‘So until where is a limit of that which, if she were to seek it, it would be for her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she had gifted it to him and entered his house, then she seeks it after that, so there is nothing for her.
It is a lot (of time) for her if she were to make him swear an oath with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that there is nothing for her with him from her dower, neither little nor more’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “

This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a husband and wife who both die and the heirs of the woman ask the heirs of the man to pay her mahr (dower). He (the Imam) said, ‘There is no such right for them/ I then asked, ‘What happens if woman is living and after his death comes and asks for her mahr (dower)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘There is nothing for her; she lived with him until his death.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if she dies and he lives and her heirs come and ask for her mahr (dower)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She lived with him until her death and did not ask.’ I said that that is true. He (the Imam) said, ‘They have no right.’
I then asked, ‘What happens if he divorces her and she asks for her mahr (dower).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She had lived with him and did not ask for her mahr (dower), so there is nothing for her.’
I then asked, ‘When has she the right to ask for her mahr (dower)?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘When she is led to his house until she arrives, her demand thereafter is nothing for her, such time is a great deal.
She can ask him to take an oath by Allah saying that he does not owe her any mahr (dower), small or large.’”
